correctness.rationale: Every idempotent of the metric partial-bijection monoid is uniquely a partial identity, giving a Boolean semilattice whose atoms force a vertex permutation. The unique inverse and all singleton restrictions determine any abstract monoid automorphism as conjugation by this permutation. Rank-two maps characterize equality of positive pair distances, giving an exact color-class normalizer. In a cycle, the distance-one class must map to a connected distance-k cycle and hence k is coprime to n, forcing affine relabeling; all affine unit maps do normalize. For a wheel the two positive distances can only be preserved, not swapped, because the wheel is not isomorphic to its complement; the unique hub and rim then give exactly the dihedral group. The stated finite enumeration verifies membership sets through n=8 cycle and n=7 wheel but is not substituted for these arguments.

value.rationale: The group of abstract automorphisms of the entire inverse monoid is a natural structural invariant distinct from the graph isometry group, and a complete family classification. The nφ(n) affine group can exceed the 2n dihedral units by arbitrarily large factors as n grows; adding one universal hub sharply removes exactly that extra distance-color symmetry for all n≥5. This mechanism is useful for identifying when a metric inverse monoid remembers numerical distance labels rather than only their equality partition.
